children: Polymarket named Warren Jenson, an executive who has led finances at a number of major corporations, as its new chief financial officer.
Jenson previously served as finance chief of Amazon, Electronic Arts, Delta Air Lines and NBC during the '90s and early 2000s.

Most recently, he was chief financial officer at Nielsen, which he left in January 2025. Before that, he spent more than four years as president and chief financial officer of the data platform LiveRamp.
Jenson is Polymarket's first company-wide finance chief, and joins at a pivotal time for the prediction markets industry.

Polymarket was one of the early entrants in the prediction markets sector, and has been sparring with Kalshi to be the top operator. Other companies, including Robinhood and DraftKings, have launched products more recently and are adding to the competition.
Polymarket is in the process of expanding its U.S. platform after gaining regulatory oversight from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
